questions.question: Which description fits the **CoverageEligibilityResponse** resource?
options: This resource provides eligibility and plan details from the processing of an CoverageEligibilityRequest resource.
This resource provides the insurance enrollment details to the insurer regarding a specified coverage.
This resource provides enrollment and plan details from the processing of an EnrollmentRequest resource.

This resource provides patient and insurance coverage information to an insurer for them to respond, in the form of an CoverageEligibilityResponse, with information regarding whether the stated coverage is…
questions.explanation: **CoverageEligibilityResponse**: This resource provides eligibility and plan details from the processing of an CoverageEligibilityRequest resource. The other descriptions belong to **EnrollmentRequest**, **EnrollmentResponse**, **CoverageEligibilityRequest**.

questions.question: Which resource matches this definition from the specification? “This resource provides eligibility and plan details from the processing of an CoverageEligibilityRequest resource.”
questions.explanation: This is the definition of **CoverageEligibilityResponse** (Financial › Support).

questions.question: Where does **CoverageEligibilityResponse** sit in the FHIR R4 resource list?
questions.explanation: **CoverageEligibilityResponse** is in **Financial › Support**: Insurance cover and enrolment: who pays for the patient’s care (Coverage), and checking eligibility before care is given.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **CoverageEligibilityResponse** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of CoverageEligibilityResponse are `status` (1..1), `purpose` (1..*), `patient` (1..1), `created` (1..1), `request` (1..1), `outcome` (1..1), `insurer` (1..1). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **CoverageEligibilityResponse** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of CoverageEligibilityResponse: `status`. `status`: active | cancelled | draft | entered-in-error. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
